newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada sees new salmon talks with U.S..
newsitem.headline: Canada sees new salmon talks with U.S..

text.p: Canada and the United States were likely to return to the bargaining table next week to resume talks on Pacific salmon fishing that collapsed last month, Canada's Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said on Thursday.
"We feel we could get back to the table next week, but I'll know more exactly by the end of this week," Axworthy told reporters after a cabinet meeting.
Canada and the United States have skirmished for years over salmon catches in the Pacific Northwest, and pressure for a deal was mounting before this year's salmon run, which begins in a few weeks.

In May the Canadians walked out on talks when U.S. negotiators said they were not authorised to offer a specific catch reduction at the session. Canada was concerned about overfishing by U.S. boats as salmon head through Alaskan waters into Canadian waters to breed.

Canada seized four U.S. boats after talks broke down last month, enforcing existing regulations against the boats as a sign of its frustrations. The boats were released after samll fines were paid, but the United States said the actions poisoned the atmosphere for discussions.

The American boats have stuck closely to Canadian regulations in the past week, however, cooling tensions between the two countries, Foreign Affairs spokeswoman Valerie Noftle said in a telephone interview.
"One of the things that is encouraging is that U.S. vessels have been closely abiding to our regulations," she said.
Axworthy said on Thursday he spoke with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright this week and was encouraged.
"I think there's an interest to restart negotiations, but we have to have another exchange," he said. "In the last discussions there was a fair degree of closure on a lot of the items."
Noftle said Canada had always been willing to return to the bargaining table but was waiting for the United States to hold talks with stakeholders.
